I have farmed this land a long time, and I do not change too much unless there is a clear reason. On 12 mu with well irrigation, I will keep the wheat-maize system as the backbone because it is steady and fits my experience, and I will keep some cotton because I already know how to manage it and it spreads risk. I will put 8 mu into winter wheat followed by summer maize, and 4 mu into cotton. I do not study fancy methods, so I will use the kinds of seed and field practices that are reliable for me: improved wheat seed, hybrid maize, and improved cotton seed. Because I have irrigation from a well, I will water at the key times instead of gambling on rainfall. I will use moderate fertilizer, not the heaviest rate, because I want stable yields and I do not want to waste money. I will use rotary tillage because it is practical on my scale and fits the way I prepare land. I will spray pesticides only as much as needed to keep pests and disease from getting ahead of me. My goal is not to chase the very highest yield. I want a stable year, manageable labor, and crops I know I can bring to harvest.
